name: Rocket Propulsion
description: This course provides an in-depth study of the fundamentals of rocket propulsion, including thermodynamics of the combustion chamber and nozzle. Students analyze solid, liquid, and hybrid rocket motors and apply propulsion theory to engine performance.

name: Aerodynamics
description: This course explores the principles of aerodynamics and how airflow interacts with wings, airfoils, and other flying bodies. Students study lift, drag, compressible flow, and the aerodynamic considerations used in aircraft and spacecraft design.

name: Spacecraft Design
description: This course covers the principles of spacecraft design, including structures, propulsion, thermal control, and power systems. Students apply systems engineering methods to mission design, orbital mechanics, and payload integration for current and future space missions.

name: Orbital Mechanics
description: This course introduces the principles of orbital mechanics, including Kepler's laws, orbital elements, and spacecraft trajectory analysis. Students learn to calculate transfer orbits, rendezvous maneuvers, and interplanetary trajectories for space missions.

name: Organic Chemistry
description: This course introduces the structure, properties, and reactions of carbon-based compounds. Students study functional groups, reaction mechanisms, and stereochemistry, and apply them to synthesis problems.
